title: A Seat at the Table
tagline: You don't need a platform to change someone's life. You need a table.
seo_title: A Seat at the Table: Jesus, Meals and Presence | Matthew 9 for Men | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Jesus didn't wait for people to get their lives together; He met them over a meal. A devotional on Matthew 9:9-13 and Mark 10:43-45 about serving with presence.
verse_text: Go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice.' For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.

scriptures.text: Go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice.' For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.
Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant... For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.

blocks.text: You don't just eat to be full. You eat to be formed.
Meals were never meant to be private. They were meant to be shared. Not just for food, but for connection, for healing, for transformation.
You don't just need nourishment. You need people. And someone needs you.
Jesus didn't just preach in temples. He sat at tables with tax collectors, with sinners, with the overlooked and the unwanted. While religious people kept their distance, Jesus pulled up a chair.
Matthew 9 shows us something powerful.
Jesus didn't wait for people to get their lives together. He met them over a meal.
Meals disarm people. Walls come down. Conversations open up. Hearts soften.
Then in Mark 10, Jesus flips the script on greatness. Not power, status or recognition, but service. And not surface-level service, but self-giving service.
Connect the two. Jesus didn't serve people from a distance. He sat with them. He gave time, attention and presence, not just answers.
Most men miss this in one of two ways. There's the Isolated Grinder: "I'll eat, work and live on my own." And there's the Occasional Helper: "I'll serve when it's convenient."
Jesus shows a different way: the Present Servant. Not just doing things for people, but being with people.
Real impact doesn't happen at a distance. It happens across tables, in conversations and in shared moments.
Jesus' ministry looked like walking, talking, eating and serving, over and over again. He didn't rush people. He didn't treat people like projects. He made time for them.
And then He said, "Now you do the same."
You don't need a platform to change someone's life. You need a table.
A meal can open a heart. A conversation can shift a life. A moment can change a direction.
When you serve others, you are formed. Not just them. You.

items: Who am I doing life around, but not actually with?
When was the last time I slowed down long enough to really see someone?
Who in my life needs a seat at my table?
Where have I made life about efficiency instead of people?
I will not rush past people.
Greatness is not what I gain.
It's who I give myself to.

blocks.text: Today, keep it simple. Invite someone to eat with you, or to sit, talk or grab coffee. No pressure, just presence.
While you're with them, put your phone away, ask real questions and listen fully. Look for one way to serve them in that moment. Not big. Just intentional.
I don't just eat to be full. I eat to build people.
